text:
mira: quick thread — Customer Y wants a fast opt-in to an edge routing canary for 12 tenants. needs per-tenant opt-in/skiplist, A/B on prompt variants, and a short rollback window. can we scope a safe minimal plan?
ajay: region-based edge routing vs dedicated edge nodes? which one?
sam: they asked region-level to avoid extra hop; means routing rule + regional fallback.
toni: risks: cold KV cache, telemetry gaps on new slice, token-spend spikes. ops: per-tenant kill-switch and quota guard.
mira: minimal proposal: 1) customer-controlled skiplist 2) 5% sampling to prompt-B 3) per-tenant kill-switch endpoint + reason code 4) telemetry hooks for 95p latency and token delta 5) short eval on first 500 responses.
ajay: config stub:
```nflag=edge_opt_quick_v1; rules: tenant in ["y-001","y-002"] -> route=edge; tenant in skiplist -> route=regional; sampling=0.05; kill=POST /api/flags/edge_opt_quick_v1/kill; approve=POST /api/flags/edge_opt_quick_v1/approve
```
sam: ramp plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 24h with telemetry gates and manual approval option for "fast-opt". checks: latency_95p, token_per_req, quick quality eval.
toni: fallback order: 1) regional compatible model 2) quantized cheaper variant + notify customer 3) 503 with friendly message. auto-stepdown if token spend >2x baseline in 2h.
ops-bot: approval requested by mira for y-001 fast-opt. status: pending.
mira: owners: @ajay build kill-switch+approve endpoint (ETA 3h), @sam dashboard+small eval job (ETA 5h), @toni write auto-fallback rules (ETA EOD). require SRE on-call for fast-opt and manual approvals at each ramp step first hour. reconvene in 6h for go/no-go. :thumbsup:
